I think the issue is with their 4G services. 5G SA for Starhub and M1 should be similar.
M1 is using 4G and 5G SA, they do not operate 5G NSA, so there is no seamless transition. Whereas like Singtel MVNOs and Simba, they all have 5G NSA, which technically is using 4G cell and upgrade it to 5G.
Hence, when one is out of 5G SA area, the connection goes out, and you don't automatically connect back, hence the aeroplane mode.

In Wifi calling, the phone makes a VPN to the provider's gateway.

5G/4G or ios/Android should not matter as far as your wifi is concern (the gateway side can choose to reject)

post_text:
The 5¢ / 6¢ / 7¢ deductions from prepaid -- have been discussed for years (this thread started in 2019 !!)
This (same) discussion has also occurred on various other HWZ threads -- including on the
'most valued prepaid card' thread
.
Without repeating everything that has (already) been previously discussed...
-- This "weird" / "unknown" 5¢ / 6¢ / 7¢ deductions from prepaid is usually due to VoLTE access.
If you port to Starhub prepaid, VoLTE is also available on Starhub prepaid.
@crystalnox
already
shared (in Jan '23) that he also encountered 5¢ deduction on Starhub prepaid when VoLTE is enabled
. See below post:
This (usually) occurs when
:
(i) You don't buy data plan for your prepaid line.
(ii) AND your phone successfully access / connect to VoLTE (on 4G) for your prepaid line.
The most obvious "solutions" are
:
(1) Buy data plan for your prepaid line.
(But not everyone buys & continuously renews data plan for their prepaid line.)
(2) Avoid VoLTE completely OR disable mobile data for your prepaid line.
(2a) Use a 4G phone that doesn't support VoLTE for your (telco's) prepaid line.
(2b) Set your phone to use 3G only -- i.e. no VoLTE access at all since VoLTE only works on 4G.
(2c)
Disable mobile data
for your prepaid line
at the telco side
.
If you previously used an older 3G only prepaid SIM card, you're effectively enjoying "solution" (2b) -- i.e. your prepaid line connects to 3G only, NEVER access / connects to VoLTE (on 4G) -- that's why previously you never encounter the 5¢ / 6¢ / 7¢ deductions from your prepaid line
.
(Once you upgrade to a 4G prepaid SIM card & access / connection to VoLTE occurs, the cents deduction from your prepaid starts. This is what
@dagobah
discovered -- see
his post earlier in this thread
.)
The
added problem now
is that
3G telco networks in SG will be shutdown on 2024-07-31
(less than 6 mths from now).
This means
solution (2b) above is not viable after 2024-07-31
.
O
nce 3G is shutdown
, all phone connections to telco networks will be on 4G (or 5G) & that means
VoLTE
(or VoNR)
MUST be used if you wish to make or receive mobile calls on your prepaid line after 2024-07-31
.
If you don't intend to use mobile data at all -- for your prepaid line,
-- You can do (2c), i.e. disable data for your prepaid line at the telco side.
But some people discover that..
They have problem / can't connect to VoLTE on their phones -- once they switch / upgrade to a 4G prepaid SIM card (from a previous 3G prepaid SIM card) -- while (2c) is still maintained, i.e. mobile data is still disabled for their prepaid line at the telco side,
(There is also no one single solution --- to resolve the issue when there's no VoLTE access on your phone -- since VoLTE support for different telcos vary between different model of phones.)
Yes, it's a mess.
From above, it is clear that the "solution" to the issue of 5¢ / 6¢ / 7¢ deductions on prepaid -- vary from person-to-person -- i.e. no 1 single solution applies to everyone.
It depends on:
- Whether you (regularly) buy & renew data plan on your prepaid line.
- Whether you need to make & receive calls on your prepaid line (especially after 2024-07-31) or just use your prepaid for simple purposes only e.g. just to receive OTP SMS.

I have been using Singtel MVNOs since Nov 2019, was on GOMO, Zero1 and currently Zym Mobile. My experience has been the same throughout the years, which is heavy speed throttling during peak hours. 1) Other people's ONR will not work for Singtel TV Box. For all local ISPs, the ONT/ONR are tagged to specific subscriber (activated by the backend) and not interchangeable.

FTP 1 --> Singtel ONR in DB Box -- Ethernet Cable 1 --> Singtel TV Box in living room console area

4) Some more advanced users use VLAN capable switch to use single Ethernet Cable to combine Singtel TV with other ISP. This is a more advanced topic and you may want to search the forum for the configuration. You need to have two VLAN capable switch.

Hello nice to meet you. I recently got a whizcomms contract and I have this weird habit of messing with things im not supposed to.
This is a tutorial on how to extract your SIP credentials from your Singtel XS-240X-A ONR.
In order to use this, you need to have a Singtel Digital Voice line
Firstly, you need to make a backup of your current configuration and store it somewhere in a folder.
You then need to go to this github repository and follow the instructions there.
https://github.com/khehshhs/nokia-xs-240x-a-cfg-decrypt/tree/main
Once you get the XML file, you can start searching for your SIP credentials by using ctrl + f to find this.
<SIP. n="VoiceLineSip" t="staticObject">
<AuthUserName dv="" ml="128" rw="RW" t="string" v="+65
You then can find the SIP credentials in the AuthUserName and AuthPassword field.
Alright and also you need to bridge vlan 30 to a free lan port to get access to their SIP server.
You just need to go the router webui and go to "Network", then "WAN" and create a new connection.
Then you need to do the following,
Tick the checkbox "Enable/Disable".
Tick "Enable VLAN" checkbox.
IP mode: Add svlan
VLAN ID: 30
VLAN Pri: 6
LAN Port binding --> Tick the lan port of your choice.
Then click "SAVE".
After all of that, you can connect any device that is capable of using this SIP service and vims.singtel.com is the server and the port is 5060. The outbound proxy is moip.oc2 and the credentials are the credentials that you have just extracted.

thread_title: Anyone is also using the StarHub UltraSpeed (10Gbps)? I am so frustrated. (Solved by upgrading ONR firmware.)
post_text:
Updated on July 20: ONR (Nokia XS-250X-A, Black) reboot issue has been solved by upgrading ONR's firmware.
StarHub was finally aware this issue was not alone and asked Nokia for a solution. Then Nokia gave this latest firmware, and it did help.
Original post below:
I applied for StarHub's UltraSpeed/10Gbps when I moved into my new home in early March. I guess I am an early bird in this plan. I even posted here to understand the speed of different ISP before choosing the plan. But, StarHub's new 10Gbps plan attracted me. Finally, I realized that stability is much more important than speed. I didn't expect that stability would be a problem in 2023.
After I set up my broadband, I found that sometimes my internet was lost, and it happened frequently (at least 3 times per day on average). Firstly, I doubt it was the Fiber connection issue. But, finally, I found it was caused by the ONR. It randomly reboots itself, and the connection will be lost when it reboots. (I found the login info on a label pasted on the ONR. Every time the connection was lost, I found the "Device Running Time" was reset and showed "0 hours x minutes x seconds" after I logged into the ONR admin).
Then, I called StarHub and told them about this issue. They sent a technician and changed the ONR for me at the end of March. Unfortunately, it didn't help.
After that, I realized it was not because one certain ONR had a fault. Either this model is not qualified, or another problem caused its reboot. I decided to seek the reason in myself. Then, I bought kinds of fans and tried to blow the ONR 7x24 and placed it in another place to better the heat dissipation. But it didn't help. Even when the aircon was turned on and the temperature was quite low, it still rebooted sometimes. I realized I could not solve this issue by myself.
After a couple of business trips abroad, I returned home this month and asked for help from StarHub. So,
Jun 13: I called StarHub and told them my connection issue was not solved after changing the ONR at the end of March. They asked me to turn off the ONR and plug out and in all cables. And they helped me do some reconfiguration (I actually didn't understand what they did. But my public IP was changed after that.) and asked me to monitor if the issue was solved. It didn't help, and the ONR still rebooted after that.
Jun 14: I called them and told them the issue still occurred. Then they told me they would arrange for a senior technician to help me.
Jun 15: A technician came and would like to change the ONR again. I told him I had already changed it once in March and it didn't help. Then, he thought it most likely would not help (it seems he didn't know this background). But there was nothing he could do but change it. So, I let him change it again with the same model. But I got a piece of interesting information from him that StarHub is providing another model of ONR for all new customers of UltraSpeed. It is a white Nokia ONR with WiFi ability. He told me that if it didn't help, I should call them and ask for that new model to have a try. Sure enough, it didn't help.
Jun 16: I told them changing the ONR with the same model didn't help. Please try to change with another new model next time. They told me they would send a technician on Sunday (Jun 18). I finally see hope since I guess the instability of my old ONR caused this problem.
Jun 18: A technician came with the same old model and tried to change it for the third time. Then I told him the context, and I refused to change it. He told me that he would escalate this issue and someone would call me back.
Jun 19: Someone from StarHub called me back and understood my issue after I explained it to him. I told him that the easiest way is having me the new model to have a try. He told me that the new model is for a new plan that is different from mine and someone would call me back 2 days later.
Jun 21: Someone called me back and asked me again about the issue. I explained again and he told me someone would call me back the next day. (I was shocked.)
Jun 22: A call rang for at most 3 seconds. It hung up after I picked up the phone. And one SMS came in immediately and said they tried to contact me and could not reach me. They would call me again the next day.
Jun 23 (Yesterday): A man called me and asked whether the modem or the router rebooted, and the router was Linksys or Nokia... (Actually, almost every time they asked me the same question, I needed to explain that the UltraSpeed plan differs from your 1Gbps/2Gpbs plans. There is no separate modem or router. It is an ONR...) Then, he told me to plug out and in all cables and they will monitor it and call me back the next day.
Jun 24 (Today), I found the ONR rebooted again at around 01:58 when my mobile game told me my connection was lost.
Any suggestions? Thanks a lot.
